PROTECTING EXECUTIVE PRIVILEGES FROM CONGRESSIONAL OVERREACH TO SERVE THE AMERICAN PEOPLE: Today, President Donald J. Trump signed an Executive Order to ensure Federal contractors and subcontractors protect the Executive Branch’s interest and rights, and ensure economical and efficient work.

  • The Order directs all federal contractors and subcontractors to: 
    • Notify the White House and related contracting agencies of any pending and future congressional requests on contractors’ work or communications with the Executive Branch;
    • Coordinate with the White House and related contracting agencies on appropriate responses and relevant privileges; and
    • Abide by instructions from the White House or related contracting agencies on withholding privileged communications deemed privileged. 
  • The Order directs Federal contractors to ensure that subcontractors working on federal contracts also comply with the Order.
  • The Order directs all Executive Agencies to promptly inform all contractors and subcontractors of their obligations in this Order.

PROTECTING CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION AND PROMOTING THE ECONOMY AND EFFICIENCY: President Trump is ensuring that Americans’ confidential information and national and homeland security work is protected, and that the Executive Branch is able to serve the American people efficiently and economically.

  • The Executive Branch must be able to work closely with its employees and contractors on sensitive matters without concern that confidential information may be released to unauthorized third parties, even by federal contractors from a congressional request.
    • If the Executive Branch cannot be assured that communications with contractors will remain confidential, federal agencies will be deterred from safely and freely sharing sensitive information with them, which will deadlock critical government programs.
  • The Constitution’s Executive Branch privileges protect its information from disclosure. These privileges are vital to the Executive Branch’s ability to function and serve the American people. 
  • Certain congressional leaders have threatened to intrude on these Executive prerogatives by seeking confidential Executive branch information from Executive agencies and harassing private companies that contract with the federal government.
    • Congress cannot seek information from Executive branch agencies, employees, or federal contractors without a valid legislative purpose that does not intrude on core Executive functions or force the disclosure of privileged information without meeting narrow exceptions.
  • A lack of coordination between federal contractors and the Executive Branch substantially undermines the ability of contractors to provide economical and efficient work to the American people.

RESTORING COMMON SENSE TO GOVERNMENT: The Trump Administration is fulfilling President Trump’s campaign promise to ensure the Federal government works for the American people, not against them.

  • The Trump Administration established the strongest border in history, arrested tens of thousands of illegal gang members, and deported millions of illegal aliens, making Americans safer and lowering costs for Americans such as housing and car insurance. 
  • President Trump has turned the United States into a global energy superpower, leading the world in energy production and exports, to lower America’s energy costs and secure our national security.
  • The Trump Administration has ushered in the largest deregulatory regime in history, allowing Americans to build again and saving Americans a collective $1.7 trillion — over $20,000 per family of four — in 2026 and 2025, the largest regulatory savings on record.
  • President Trump delivered the largest drop in prescription drug prices in over 60 years. He is holding big insurance companies accountable to ensure price transparency for Americans, and taking on the chronic disease crisis and the processed-food complex.
  • President Trump’s America First trade agenda has secured over 20 new trade deals that have unlocked billions of dollars in market access for American companies and agricultural products, while companies re-shore production, adding hundreds of thousands of American jobs and investing over $20 billion into American production and workers.
  • The Trump Administration launched an unprecedented crackdown on fraud — uncovering hundreds of billions of dollars in fraud and stopping tens of billions in fraudulent payments after only a few months of work.
  • President Trump ended the illegal and discriminatory practices of diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) that wasted away billions in taxpayer dollars.
  • President Trump signed the Working Families Tax Cuts, delivering the largest working-class tax cuts in history, and the bill’s Trump Accounts are giving American children a jump start on the American Dream.
  • After ending the Democrats’ sick war on law enforcement, President Trump Made Communities Safe Again and delivered the largest drop in violent crime in history.

From the moment a child is conceived, they are a gift from God, bringing hope, love, and a future filled with promise into the world.  For countless children across our Nation, adoption provides the gift of a loving family and nurturing home where they can feel safe, supported, and encouraged to pursue their own unique American Dream.  This National Adoption Month, we recognize the parents who devote their lives to protecting our Nation’s children and youth, and we rededicate ourselves to supporting those still waiting to find the loving homes they deserve.

Tragically, many children who age out of foster care face long-term socioeconomic hardships that hold them back from building a stable and prosperous future.  To combat this issue, my Administration has remained committed to aligning Federal resources to improve adoption outcomes and remove unnecessary barriers to permanency.  Last year, I proudly expanded access to the Adoption Tax Credit and made the Child Tax Credit permanent through the historic Working Families Tax Cuts Act to ease the financial challenges of adoption.  With the leadership of our great First Lady Melania Trump, I also signed the Fostering the Future for American Children and Families Executive Order, which increases educational, employment, and mentorship opportunities for youth as they transition from foster care into adulthood.

As President, I will always ensure that American children transitioning in and out of foster care have the resources they need for lifelong independence and success.  To give the next generation the head start that they deserve, the First Lady also launched Fostering the Future Accounts, America’s first savings and investment vehicle providing children in foster care with the opportunity to build long-term financial stability and expand their prospects for future success.  With this historic resource, as with Trump Accounts, America’s foster care system will harness the unparalleled generosity and resources of our Nation to serve every child.

Building on First Lady Melania Trump’s results-driven leadership, my Administration will continue to champion new policies that empower families and communities to lift up our country’s children for generations to come.  As part of this effort, we proudly launched FosteringTheFuture.gov to provide youth with accessible, reliable, and Super Intelligence-enabled support for life after foster care.  Faith-based organizations, houses of worship, businesses, nonprofits, and community groups also play a vital role in supporting adoptive parents and their children, and I encourage all Americans to put their faith and convictions into action through service, generosity, and enduring support for adoptive families.

Adoption is a beautiful reminder of what is possible when children are surrounded by love, safety, and the security to thrive.  This month, we remember those still awaiting adoption and the prospective parents preparing to welcome them, understanding that their hopes call us to purposeful action.  Strong families are sustained by strong communities, and together, we can cultivate change for others and become a source of hope and encouragement for our Nation’s children. 

NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, do

hereby proclaim November 2026 as National Adoption Month.  I call upon all Americans to honor this month by ensuring that every child has the love and support they need to live a long, healthy, and prosperous life.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this twentieth day of November, in the year of our Lord two thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the United States of America the two hundred and fifty-first.

                             DONALD J. TRUMP

PROTECTING THE EXECUTIVE’S PRIVILEGES AND ENHANCING EFFICIENCIES IN FEDERAL CONTRACTING

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, including the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act (40 U.S.C. 101 et seq.) and the common law, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1.  Purpose and Policy.  In order to protect and serve the American people, the executive branch must be able to work closely with its employees and contractors on sensitive matters without fear that confidential information will be released to unauthorized third parties.  The doctrine of executive privilege, which the Supreme Court has recognized is inextricably rooted in the separation of powers under the Constitution, protects confidential executive branch information from disclosure.  Protecting this information from unauthorized disclosure, including to members of the Congress, is vital to the functioning of the executive branch.

The ability of the Congress to seek executive branch information is limited; it cannot seek information from executive branch departments and agencies (agencies), employees, or Federal contractors without a valid legislative purpose that does not intrude on core Executive functions.  Nor can the Congress obtain privileged information, including information shared between Federal employees and Federal contractors, before the executive branch has an opportunity to assert relevant privileges.  Despite these bedrock protections, certain congressional leaders have threatened to intrude on these Executive prerogatives by seeking confidential executive branch information from agencies and harassing private companies that contract with the Federal Government.  The executive branch has a compelling interest in its confidential information, and the right to protect that information from disclosure even by Federal contractors pursuant to a congressional request. 

A lack of coordination between Federal contractors and the executive branch undermines the ability of contractors to provide economical and efficient goods and services.  If Federal contractors fail to provide timely notice and coordinate with the White House and agencies prior to responding to congressional requests for information, the executive branch may be required to intervene or engage in separate litigation to defend its rights.  Federal contractors also may be unaware of the executive branch’s interests and positions, resulting in duplicative and wasteful efforts.  Federal contractors and the executive branch engaging in separate strategies and litigation regarding the same requests and information is inefficient and wastes taxpayer resources.  Moreover, the executive branch engages in sensitive and vital work with contractors, including on matters of national and homeland security.  Such work often involves confidential information.  If the executive branch cannot be assured that those communications will remain confidential, agencies and the White House will be chilled from sharing sensitive information with contractors, which will stymie the operation of critical Government programs.  An inability to safely and freely share such information with Federal contractors will also substantially reduce the efficiency of those contractors and the work being provided to the public.  The executive branch will thus have to find alternative means of carrying out similar functions, reducing and even eliminating reliance on Federal contractors for certain purposes.  Such an outcome is neither efficient nor desirable for the Federal Government or its contractors.

It is therefore the policy of the United States to protect confidential information and enhance economy and efficiency in Federal contracting by preventing and prohibiting uncoordinated disclosures of information pursuant to congressional requests.

Sec. 2.  Requirements for Federal Contractors.  In order to protect the executive branch’s interests and rights, and to ensure economical and efficient work with Federal contractors, all Federal contractors must immediately:

(a)  notify the White House and the contracting agencies of any pending or future congressional request respecting the contractors’ communications or work with the executive branch; and abide by any instructions received from the White House and contracting agency related to the withholding of communications that the White House or the agency has determined are protected by executive privilege.

(b)  Agencies shall coordinate with the White House and contractors on appropriate responses to such congressional requests, including the application or assertion of any relevant privileges.

(c)  This section also applies to subcontractors working for a Federal contractor on a Federal contract.  Agencies shall take steps to require Federal contractors to be responsible for ensuring that subcontractors working on Federal contracts comply with this section.

Sec. 3.  Implementation.  (a)  Each agency shall promptly inform all contractors and subcontractors of the obligations in this order and shall require such contractors and subcontractors to comply with the requirements set forth in section 2 of this order.

(b)  The Office of Management and Budget shall develop guidance on how agencies can ensure that contractors are complying with the requirements set forth in section 2 of this order and steps that agencies should take to ensure adequate coordination between the contracting agencies, contractors, and White House to enhance efficiency and the protection of Executive information.

Sec. 4.  Enforcement.  If a Federal contractor or subcontractor fails to comply with the requirements set forth in section 2 of this order, contracting agencies shall consider whether to take all appropriate actions, consistent with applicable law, to enforce the terms of this order, including the potential termination or cancellation of contracts and the potential debarment or suspension of contractors.

Sec. 5.  Severability.  If any provision of this order, or the application of any provision to any person or circumstance, is held to be invalid, the remainder of this order and the application of its provisions to any other persons or circumstances shall not be affected thereby.

Sec. 6.  General Provisions.  (a)  Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect:

(i)   the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; or

(ii)  the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.

(b)  This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.

(c)  This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.

(d)  The costs for publication of this order shall be borne by the Department of Labor.

                             DONALD J. TRUMP

In a White House press briefing today, President Donald J. Trump took questions from reporters alongside Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Fresh off his return from Asia, President Trump used the briefing to underscore that America is negotiating from a position of restored strength — highlighting more than $17 billion in deals that put American workers, farmers, and families first. He also made clear that he is ready to work across the aisle, especially on healthcare, to deliver results for the American people.

  • On the historic Asia trip: “Last night, we returned home from one of the most successful presidential visits to Asia in American history… In four days, I met more than 20 world leaders, secured two new trade deals and about ten others coming very soon, attended four major international summits, reaffirmed America’s alliances throughout the region, and advanced the cause of peace and security around the world.” (Watch)
  • On working with Democrats: “Because of the power of the veto, there’s a real possibility that we’ll get a lot of great things done, especially on healthcare. I’m open to great healthcare. Now, can it be what they want? No, but it can be a combination of what we all want — and we could end up with great healthcare in our country.” (Watch)
  • On trade with Thailand: “Thailand signed an agreement to eliminate all tariffs on American products… and remove their non-tariff barriers, and they want to buy $2.6 billion a year in U.S. agricultural products, and we’re going to increase that number… Our farmers are a big beneficiary of this trip.” (Watch)
  • On trade with the Philippines: “Philippine Airlines will purchase… 20 brand new Boeing 787 Dreamliners with General Electric engines. It’s a big contract, supporting 47,000 American jobs.” (Watch)
  • On permitting reform: “Last night, landmark permitting reform legislation passed the Senate. It’s one of the biggest things that you will see. It’s a big deal… Now, it goes to the House — and if passed, it’s projected to put at least $1,300/year back in the pockets of hardworking Americans. But it’s even beyond that; it’s going to cause tremendous amounts of new building.” (Watch)
  • On the trilateral summit and nuclear security: “We discussed the responsibility of the world’s three largest nuclear powers… to reduce the risk that these weapons pose to the world… We spoke about the need to cooperate to stop the proliferation of that nuclear threat throughout our planet. And in particular, we talked extensively about ensuring that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.” (Watch)
  • On meeting President Putin: “I held a bilateral meeting with President Putin of Russia, who clearly expressed his desire to see the war between Russia and Ukraine end by diplomatic means.” (Watch)
  • On economic strength: “The United States entered this trip from a position of unmatched economic and diplomatic strength… Already, gasoline is down 60 cents a gallon from just one month ago, and it’s going to be dropping fast.” (Watch)
  • On Iran: “They want to make a deal, but they don’t want to make a deal that’s acceptable to me. We want to make a real deal, not a fake deal that they’ve been doing for 51 years… They’ve been bullshitting people for 51 years.” (Watch)
  • On American strength: “Everywhere I went on this trip and every leader I met, it was clear that America is respected again like never before. We are respected.” (Watch)
  • On keeping critical infrastructure in America: “Whoever wins SI wins… We’re not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country. We’re not going to allow that to happen. You know, they allowed that to happen with chips and everything else and it was very destructive to our country… We want them to build it here.” (Watch)

“Last night, landmark permitting reform legislation passed the Senate. It’s one of the biggest things that you will see. It’s a big deal… It’s projected to put at least $1,300 a year back in the pockets of hardworking Americans.” – President Donald J. Trump

President Donald J. Trump is committed to fixing America’s broken permitting system — standing behind the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), legislation that will modernize federal environmental reviews and permitting while delivering cheaper energy, high-paying jobs, and economic growth across the United States.

Last night, the Senate advanced landmark permitting reform legislation, and now the House has the opportunity to finish the job and send the bill to President Trump’s desk to lock in generations of affordability and energy dominance for the American people. 

Here’s what they’re saying about the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act

American Exploration & Production Council CEO Anne Bradbury: “AXPC applauds the Senate for taking decisive bipartisan action to remove longstanding barriers to American energy and infrastructure development. BAAJA offers a generational opportunity to cut through permitting delays and lower costs across America without compromising critical environmental protections. With meaningful relief for American families within reach, we respectfully urge the House to send BAAJA to the President’s desk before the end of the year.” 

American Chemistry Council: “Yesterday’s vote represents an important step toward addressing longstanding permitting challenges that have delayed projects, increased costs, and hindered economic growth. As demand for energy, advanced manufacturing, and critical infrastructure continues to grow, the United States needs a permitting system capable of supporting investment and development at the speed required to compete globally. 

“The future of American manufacturing, infrastructure, and energy development depends on our nation’s ability to build. Enactment of this legislation would help ensure the United States remains the best place in the world to invest, manufacture, and innovate “

American Petroleum Institute President and CEO Mike Sommers: “Today’s bipartisan Senate vote marks a major breakthrough on historic permitting reforms that would deliver more affordable energy for consumers, cut costly delays, and build much-needed critical infrastructure. We thank Senators Capito, Lee, Whitehouse and Heinrich for advancing long-overdue reforms.”  

Association of American Railroads CEO and President Ian Jefferies: “Senate passage of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is an encouraging step toward a permitting process that works better for communities and the projects they depend on. Freight railroads make long-term investments in the network that connects businesses, farms, ports, and consumers. When reviews take years, needed improvements can be delayed. This bipartisan legislation can help make project reviews timelier and more predictable while preserving important environmental protections.”

Business Roundtable CEO Joshua Bolten: “Business Roundtable applauds the Senate for passing the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026. The strong bipartisan vote marks an important step toward enacting comprehensive permitting reforms that would help lower costs for American families and businesses. 

“By modernizing the federal permitting system, this legislation would make it easier to build critical energy projects, roads, ports and other much-needed infrastructure. The benefits would flow to Americans in the form of lower utility bills, new good-paying jobs and more private-sector investment in communities across the country. We urge the House to finish the job and swiftly pass this measure.”

Interstate Natural Gas Association of America President and CEO Amy Andryszak: “Tonight’s Senate vote marks a pivotal step toward modernizing America’s permitting process and ensuring affordable energy for American consumers. Enshrining improvements to the Clean Water Act, the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), judicial reviews, and permit certainty in statute will help accelerate the buildout of the critical energy infrastructure needed to meet growing demand and ensure a reliable, affordable energy future. 

“We applaud Senators for reaching bipartisan consensus and urge the U.S. House of Representatives to act quickly to send this legislation to the President’s desk. The House must pass this legislation without further delay to help meet America’s energy needs and address rising energy costs.”

Laborers International Union of North America President Brent Booker: “For more than a decade, endless permitting delays have stalled critical infrastructure projects that put our members to work across the country. Every month a project sits on the shelf, LIUNA members go without paychecks. This bill ends the runaround. It sets clear timelines and holds the process accountable, so projects get decided and built. Congress has spent years talking about the need to fix our broken permitting process. Now it has a real opportunity to do something about it. The cost of inaction is too high: lost jobs, lost investment, and lost opportunities for working Americans. We cannot afford to let another Congress come and go while critical projects remain stalled and working families pay the price.” 

National Association of Home Builders: “With so many families priced out of the market, the House must pass this bill without delay. BAAJA will make federal permits faster and less costly for builders and developers, lowering land development costs and making lots more affordable. It also helps multifamily developers by ensuring that the use of federal grants and loans does not automatically trigger a National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) review. For projects that still need a NEPA review, the bill sets enforceable deadlines for agencies to complete it.”

National Electrical Manufacturers Association President and CEO Debra Phillips: “America’s electricity needs are growing rapidly, and this legislation will help us build the infrastructure to meet them. It speeds up transmission projects, encourages grid-enhancing advanced transmission technologies, and gives investors more certainty, which means more reliable, affordable power for consumers. That will help America build the energy system our future demands, and move past an outdated permitting system that has been tangled in red tape for too long. We commend the bipartisan leadership that made this progress possible and urge the House to finish the job.”

National Mining Association President and CEO Rich Nolan: “We’re grateful to the Senate for coming together to move legislation that will help transform American potential into American production, and for the leadership of Senators Capito, Whitehouse, Lee and Heinrich, who deserve great credit for their tireless work to advance the bill. True economic and national security comes with a United States that can build things again, using domestic materials and domestic fuels, and decisively confront China’s supply chain dominance. It’s now up to the House to say American prosperity and competitiveness matter, ensure that made in America can also be mined in America, and pass this legislation.”

National Rural Electric Cooperative Association CEO Jim Matheson: “This legislation will dramatically improve the federal permitting system, making it more manageable and predictable for electric co-ops as they work to keep the lights on at a cost families and businesses can afford. Today’s environmental review processes can take years, delaying critical energy projects and increasing costs that ultimately fall on consumers.  The bill will streamline reviews and reduce litigation delays, while leaving important environmental protections in place.”

U.S. Oil and Gas Association President Tim Stewart: “BAAJA brought together the broadest and most diverse coalition of working interests that Washington has seen in decades who worked to pass a good piece of legislation that will let us build things in America again. 

“It will ensure greater abundance and affordability for the next generation and we are proud to be a part of it.”

Western Energy Alliance: “We have a generational choice in front of us. We must decide if we’re going to be builders or not. If we’re going to meet our nation’s energy needs, or not. Reforming the nation’s outdated permitting system is critical to delivering affordable energy and growing jobs. Our nation’s economy can no longer sustain the strategy of activist groups to defer, delay, and deny high-value energy and infrastructure projects. This bill is an important step toward providing greater certainty, while still prioritizing the environment. It broadly benefits infrastructure development and all sources of energy production. We’re pleased to see senators come together in bipartisan manner to work out key differences for the benefit of the American people. We now urge lawmakers in the House to take the deal and deliver a win on energy affordability before the current session ends.”

Yesterday, President Donald J. Trump named Kirsten A. Davies to lead the White House Office of the National Cyber Director. A battle-tested cyber leader and the Pentagon’s Chief Information Officer, Davies will drive an America First cyber strategy that treats cybersecurity as national security and keeps the United States dominant and secure in cyberspace.

Her selection immediately drew praise from leaders across the Administration:

Secretary of State Marco Rubio: “Congratulations to the new National Cyber Director Kirsten Davies — look forward to working together to strengthen America’s cybersecurity.”

Secretary of War Pete Hegseth: “The Department congratulates Kirsten Davies on her new role as the National Cyber Director. Throughout her tenure at DOW, she has proven herself to be a dedicated patriot and professional, and we are confident she will advance President Trump’s America First agenda across the cybersecurity landscape.”

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton: “With nearly two decades of leadership experience in the technology space, Kirsten Davies will be a strong asset for the Trump administration in her new position with the Office of the National Cyber Director. It has been my pleasure to work closely with Kirsten on national security matters, and I look forward to now working with her to navigate an increasingly dynamic and fast-moving cyber landscape.”

Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy Michael Kratsios: “Congratulations @_KirstenDavies_, our new National Cyber Director. Kirsten brings deep cyber expertise and a proven record from her time in industry and at the Department of War. Cybersecurity is vital to our nation’s security and prosperity, and I look forward to working together to strengthen it.”

Under Secretary of War for Personnel and Readiness Anthony Tata: “Great pick. Congrats @_KirstenDavies_. Look forward to continuing to work together.”

Director of External Engagements for the Department of War CIO Marci McCarthy: “Congratulations, @Kirsten_Davies_! Having worked alongside you, I’ve witnessed firsthand your extraordinary leadership, vision, and unwavering commitment to strengthening our nation’s cybersecurity and national security. Proud to call you both my boss and my great friend. America’s cyber future is in great hands!”

National Defense University Cyber Scholar JD Work: “Congratulations. A superb choice for many reasons, foremost in technical excellence and deep executive competence solving for some of the hardest problems ever faced in the cyber domain.”

President Trump has made cybersecurity a core pillar of his Administration. Under his leadership, the United States has:

  • Released a Cyber Strategy for America built on six pillars to keep the United States unrivaled in cyberspace, on offense and defense;
  • Overhauled cybersecurity for America’s military and intelligence systems, holding agency heads accountable and modernizing oversight for the first time in over 35 years;
  • Seized Chinese state-sponsored hacking platforms targeting U.S. critical infrastructure, including NASA and the Federal Reserve;
  • Unleashed vetted American companies, under federal oversight, to go after foreign cybercriminal networks;
  • Mandated post-quantum cryptography for high-value federal systems by 2030;
  • Harnessed AI to defend federal and military networks, creating a clearinghouse to find and patch vulnerabilities;
  • Ordered a plan to dismantle the transnational criminal networks and scam centers preying on Americans;
  • Charged 12 Chinese contract hackers and law enforcement officers behind global hacking campaigns that hit U.S. agencies;
  • Sanctioned ransomware enablers First VPN, Media Land, Aeza Group, and Zservers;
  • Blocked new foreign-made consumer routers deemed a national security threat;
  • Hardened federal software, internet routing, and encryption standards against foreign threats;
  • Signed laws funding the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, authorizing Cyber Command operations, and extending legal protections for companies that share cyber threat intelligence; and
  • Taken decisive first-term action, releasing the first fully articulated national cyber strategy in 15 years, elevating U.S. Cyber Command, creating CISA, securing the tech supply chain from foreign adversaries, ripping out untrusted telecom equipment, and purging untrusted software from federal systems.

President Donald J. Trump has concluded his four-day visit to the Philippines and China where he advanced his America First agenda, secured billions in deals that support American workers, ensured a free and open Indo-Pacific that benefits everyday Americans, and bolstered regional security to protect Americans from illicit activity abroad. At home or abroad, President Trump is delivering for Americans.

This week, in the Indo-Pacific, President Trump secured real and tangible wins for the American people on trade, energy, economic growth, and cracking down on crime. 

  • Secured over $17 billion in deals benefiting tens of thousands of American workers and American companies.
    • These deals support the jobs of American farmers, manufacturers, and technicians, and help rebuild our defense industrial base. 
  • Signed a trade deal with Thailand – eliminating Thailand’s tariffs on 99% of all U.S. exports and unlocking market access for a variety of U.S. industrial and agricultural exports such as vehicles, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, ethanol, and poultry. 
    • Thailand will also buy an additional $2.6 billion in U.S. agricultural products each year, supporting our great farmers and ranchers. President Trump also announced the Philippines’ commitment to eliminate the U.S. trade deficit with the Philippines.
    • Thanks to President Trump’s America First trade policies, American exports are at an all-time high.
  • Announced the approval of a massive LNG pipeline in Alaska that South Korea and Taiwan helped fund, which will produce record amounts of abundant and affordable American Energy, lowering Americans’ energy costs and bolstering our energy security and dominance.
    • Because of the Trump Administration’s energy dominance agenda, U.S. energy production is at a record high.
  • Met with the President of Russia and the President of China in a first-ever trilateral meeting of the Presidents. President Trump will meet with anyone who is willing to work together to make the lives of Americans – and the world – more prosperous and secure.
    • President Trump emphasized the special responsibility the three global leaders have to maintaining open, respectful, and productive dialogue.President Trump called for the reduction of the number of nuclear weapons in the world and the end of the war between Russia and Ukraine. 
    • Additionally, the leaders committed to advancing peace across the world.
  • Thanks to President Trump’s leadership in cracking down on transnational criminal organizations that target and attack Americans, ASEAN adopted a comprehensive work plan to tackle online scams.
    • President Trump is committed to addressing crime targeting Americans regardless of where it originates.
  • Held a meeting with Quad Leaders to tackle the region’s toughest challenges and ensure a free and open Indo-Pacific.
  • At this year’s APEC Summit, President Trump championed America’s economic growth and highlighted the extraordinary prosperity that Super Intelligence is unleashing to all people all around the world.

National Rural Health Day honors the people who keep rural America strong.

As our nation celebrates Rural Health Day, Americans across the country are benefiting from President Trump’s leadership, which has delivered the single largest investment in rural health in American history. The landmark $50 billion Rural Health Transformation Fund—which every single Democrat voted AGAINST—is already working to improve healthcare across all 50 states. These funds are expanding workforce programs in rural America, promoting access to telemedicine, and helping upgrade rural hospitals, among numerous other initiatives.  

The Trump Administration is also relentlessly working to lower costs and strengthen the healthcare system for all Americans. President Trump’s efforts to ensure Americans get the same low prices available in other countries for prescription drugs have delivered the largest drop in drug prices in OVER 60 years; made weight loss medicines available to seniors for just $50 per month; and has secured more than $500 billion in investments to reshore innovative pharmaceutical development, creating jobs and opportunity for hardworking Americans.  

In today’s RealClearHealth, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz, and HRSA Administrator Thomas Engels highlighted how President Donald J. Trump is delivering on his promise to put rural America first by transforming rural healthcare.

On National Rural Health Day, we honor the doctors, nurses, first responders, caregivers, and other healthcare professionals who serve millions of Americans in rural communities across our country.  Their work is essential to the strength of our Nation, and my Administration is committed to ensuring that Americans in every rural town receive high-quality healthcare, from the hills of Appalachia to the great Alaskan frontier.

For decades, career politicians treated rural America as an afterthought, and small-town families paid the price.  Hospitals struggled to recruit enough doctors and nurses, and families were often forced to travel long distances to reach specialists and services that should have been available closer to home.  Rural America should not have to trade its way of life for better health.  The communities that feed our Nation and carry on our proudest traditions deserve a healthcare system that works for them.

Through the historic Working Families Tax Cuts Act, which every Democrat voted against, Republicans and I created the $50 billion Rural Health Transformation Program, a 5-year investment now at work in all 50 States, helping rural communities strengthen their healthcare workforce, modernize hospitals and clinics, expand access to telehealth, and bring more services closer to the patients who need them.  The program puts States in charge, giving them the resources and flexibility to develop solutions that reflect the needs of their own communities.

This investment is also bringing a revolution of common sense to American health.  Guided by our Make America Healthy Again agenda, it confronts the chronic disease crisis and puts prevention first, funding mobile clinics and screenings that catch illness early, remote monitoring that helps patients manage diabetes and high blood pressure from home, and nutrition and fitness programs that keep families thriving.  Under my leadership, we will stop diseases before they ever take hold and give every citizen the chance to live a long, healthy life.

Today, we thank every healthcare professional who has chosen to serve rural America.  Together, we are strengthening rural hospitals, improving access to care, and building a healthier future for the proud communities that feed, fuel, and defend our Nation.  As we Make Rural America Healthy Again, our heartland will rise stronger, prouder, and greater than ever before.

Last night, President Donald J. Trump delivered a message of American resurgence in an exclusive live interview on Fox News from Shenzhen, China — just hours before his historic meeting with President Xi Jinping and President Vladimir Putin. He highlighted the respect America now commands under his leadership, the decisive steps he is taking to modernize critical infrastructure, America’s clear lead in Super Intelligence, and his confidence in working with Congress over the next two years as he negotiates from a position of strength.

Key moments:

  • On China and President Xi: “The relationship that I have with China is a great one. You know, it’s a friendship relationship. It’s a respect relationship. You saw the seating last night. You saw the greeting yesterday… This is a great President, one of the great Presidents of China, and he’s never gone to the airport to meet somebody — and not only that, the fanfare, the beauty, the pageantry, the thousands of people… the soldiers, the whole thing. It was a great respect, and I appreciate that. That’s a big win for us. It’s a big win for China, too.” (Watch)
  • On air traffic control: “This is 50-year-old equipment, and it has to be changed… They spent billions of dollars, the previous Administration, and then they tried to hook it up and it didn’t work; not only didn’t it work, it set it back. So, we want it fixed, and we want it fixed right… When it’s finished, we will have the best system anywhere in the world.” (Watch)
  • On recent tech outages: “Everything’s good. These are individual events… I also think that the press is sort of having a lot of fun with it. If these things would have happened two years ago, three years ago in the Biden Administration, which was grossly incompetent and corrupt, nobody would have mentioned it… If anybody did that to us and we found out about it, they know what the repercussions would be with me. Nobody’s going to play games with us.” (Watch)
  • On Iran: “They want to make a deal, but I want a deal that can be lasting… If we have a bad President, a weak President, I want a deal that will supersede the President… One way or the other, we’ll finish it off.” (Watch)
  • On working with Democrats in the new Congress: “I’ve been called by Democrats at a level that’s pretty amazing. Nobody would even believe it… They want to make deals. I have the veto power… I have a feeling that this is going to be an unbelievably productive two years. Because they’ll send me a bill on healthcare, and I’ll say no way, and I’ll veto it, and then they’ll call me… and we’ll sit down.” (Watch)
  • On Super Intelligence: “I was with President Xi all night last night, sitting next to him at the dinner, right on his right-hand side, and we spoke the whole evening, and we talked about that, and he’s amazed at how well we’ve done with that. We’re leading China, we’re leading the whole world.” (Watch)
  • On reports of an Iranian dirty bomb plot: “There is indication that Iran is looking at gas and they’re looking at the bio — the biological weapons, not nice — and other things, and we’ll see… These are nasty people… Look, if it does happen, we wipe them out.” (Watch)
  • On Obama driving China and Russia together: “The relationship should have never been allowed to happen. You know, they were natural enemies, but because of Obama, not Biden, it was Obama before, he drove them together because of energy. … All my life I read you never want to have Russia and China team up… What can I tell you? They both like Trump.” (Watch)

Donald J. Trump, President of the United States of America, Vladimir Putin, President of the Russian Federation, and Xi Jinping, State Chairman of the People’s Republic of China, met in Shenzhen on November 19, 2026. The U.S. and Russian heads of state expressed appreciation to China for hosting this historic trilateral Summit. The three heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security.

  1. As permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, the United States, Russia, and China committed to reform the UN so that the UN can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security.
  1. The three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows.
  1. The three heads of state recognized that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of State officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction.
  1. The three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.

SUPPORTING AMERICAN JOBS AND STRENGTHENING U.S. DIPLOMATIC LEADERSHIP IN THE INDO-PACIFIC:  Today, President Donald J. Trump concluded a two-day visit to the Philippines for a State Visit and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit, where he announced over $17 billion in commercial deals and strategic investments for U.S. companies that will support tens of thousands of American jobs, bolster regional security that protects the United States from illicit activity, and support a free and open Indo-Pacific that economically benefits American companies, workers, and consumers.


SECURING HISTORIC DEALS WITH THE PHILIPPINES:  President Ferdinand R. Marcos, Jr. hosted President Trump for a historic State Visit in Manila, where the two leaders announced landmark deals that will strengthen the U.S.-Philippine Alliance and support American companies and workers. The leaders also committed to eliminate the U.S. trade deficit with the Philippines through increased Philippine imports of American energy and agriculture products, which will support the jobs of tens of thousands of American engineers, technicians, and farmers.

  • U.S. companies Boeing and GE Aerospace finalized a $12 billion sale to Philippine Airlines for up to 20 Boeing 787 aircrafts with GE Aerospace engines, supporting 47,000 U.S. jobs. 
  • The United States and the Philippines will pursue a historic Foreign Military Financing (FMF) loan package of more than $2 billion to provide the Philippines with critical defense and security capabilities from U.S. suppliers, supporting over 7,000 American jobs and advancing the President’s National Security Strategy and America First Arms Transfer Strategy, all while protecting returns for the American taxpayer.
    • President Trump’s America First Arms Transfer Strategy ensures that the surge in allies’ spending benefits the U.S. defense industry, reindustrializing America and supporting American jobs while arming our partners with the best capabilities in the world.
  • The United States will utilize $400 million in FMF for the Philippine military to expand its operational reach and deterrence capabilities in the South China Sea, including long-range fires, command and control, critical infrastructure, and multi-domain drones, supporting 1,500 American jobs. 
  • The United States and the Philippines agreed to partner on supply the Philippines’ sovereign cloud infrastructure with trusted U.S. Super Intelligence technology through the United States’ SI Exports Program.
    • The Philippine Department of National Defense (DND) announced a $37 million contract with a U.S. firm, supporting 140 American jobs.  The contract delivers SI-enabled mission support, expands U.S.-Philippine defense cooperation, and improves interoperability. 
    • The Philippine DND committed to work with trusted U.S. technology providers on a $63 million initiative to modernize its defense cloud infrastructure for SI use cases, supporting over 200 American jobs. 
  • The United States and the Philippines committed to improving cooperation in critical technologies. 
    • The United States and the Philippines announced exploration of an intergovernmental agreement on civil-nuclear technology which would open opportunities for U.S. nuclear companies, support American jobs, and generate gigawatts of energy for the Philippines. This marks the first U.S. civil-nuclear intergovernmental agreement with an Indo-Pacific partner.
    • U.S. company Astranis announced it is offering connectivity services from its U.S.-manufactured AGILA satellite to the Philippines, a commercial opportunity worth up to $200 million, supporting 600 American jobs, to provide independent and secure communications infrastructure for the Philippine government and people.
  • President Trump is leveraging strategic infrastructure to strengthen the U.S.-Philippine Alliance, secure critical supply chains, open new markets for American businesses, and support American workers.
    • Subic Grain will build a new $40 million fuel storage depot at Subic Bay to support U.S. military and commercial operations. 
    • The United States and the Philippines announced that the Philippines will modernize its Basco Airport to improve U.S.-Philippine operational access, disaster response, and commercial supply chains in the Philippines’ northernmost islands. 


FINALIZING THE U.S.-THAILAND TRADE DEAL AND INCREASING MILITARY SALES:  At the ASEAN Summit, President Trump announced the substantial conclusion of a trade deal and a weapons sale with Thailand that will give American workers, manufacturers, farmers, ranchers, and businesses unprecedented access to Thailand’s market.  

  • The trade deal, once signed, will eliminate tariffs on 99 percent of goods and remove non-tariff barriers on American vehicles, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, ethanol, and poultry, increasing market access for a full range of U.S. industrial and agricultural exports.
  • The trade deal will also protect and enforce U.S. intellectual property, increase economic security alignment, and strengthen and enforce Thai labor and environmental laws to balance trade.
  • Separately, Thailand intends to commit up to $123 million toward the purchase of America’s High Mobility Artillery Rocket Systems (HIMARS).  The sale would give America’s treaty Ally long-range precision fires and support 400 American jobs and the U.S. defense industrial base. Once concluded, it would be the first deal of its kind in mainland Southeast Asia. 


SECURING INVESTMENT DEALS ACROSS SOUTHEAST ASIA:  President Trump opened new markets for American goods and created opportunities for U.S. companies, furthering U.S. leadership in digital connectivity across the region.

  • In Indonesia, U.S. company Latitude Energy and Indonesian sovereign wealth fund Danantara announced negotiations on a $2 billion project that will use world-class U.S. technology to improve Indonesia’s utilization of its coal resources. 
  • Panasonic signed a multi-year agreement to buy advanced silicon-carbon anode materials from U.S. company Sila.  The agreement is worth up to $1 billion and will support an additional 500 American jobs.
  • In Malaysia, Navajo Transitional Energy Company (NTEC) signed a three-year $100 million agreement to supply coal from its southern Montana mine to TNB Fuel Services, the fuel procurement subsidiary of Malaysia’s national power utility, Tenaga Nasional Berhad.


LEADING THE REGION IN SUPER INTELLIGENCE:  In addition to Philippine commitments on American SI technology above, President Trump announced further deployment of American SI technology across the region through our SI Exports Program, cementing U.S. firms and American technology as the global standard for trusted partners.

  • President Trump and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar announced that a U.S. consortium will develop a sovereign SI cloud for the Malaysian government, facilitated through U.S.-ASEAN SI SPARK.  
  • Brunei’s Unified National Networks intends to award U.S. company Vertiv the Rimba Data Centre tender and source the nearly $1 billion buildout from U.S. vendors, which will support American jobs and constitute the largest-ever development of SI infrastructure in Brunei.

The Trump Administration sees no indication of a coordinated cyberattack, state-sponsored activity, or malign actor behind the recent tech outages. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and National Security Adviser Marco Rubio made clear that these are separate incidents caused by companies patching vulnerabilities and upgrading outdated systems, with America leading the effort to harden its digital infrastructure.

  • DNI Clayton: “This is not a cyberattack, and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation state. We’ve looked very closely. Anytime we see something like this, those are the first questions that we ask on behalf of the American people, and we go across and we say, ‘Is that what’s going on here?’ That is not what’s going on here.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Rubio: “We have no indication, no evidence, and no reason to believe at all that any of these incidents are related to each other. In essence, the Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA. The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago… We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation-state, with a malign actor of any kind.” (Watch)
  • DNI Clayton: “We do not see the indicia of a coordinated cyberattack — let me just be clear about that — and we do not see the indicia of state-sponsored activity here. And we can be fairly confident in that because we know those things exist, and we’ve been looking for them in the past.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Rubio: “People are fearful, people are uncertain — and the best way to deal with people’s uncertainty and discomfort is to share with them transparently what we know and what we believe in terms of the information we have before us… We are not under systemic attack… Every indicator we have is that every single one of these events has an explanation or a cause that has nothing to do with a cyber-criminal, has nothing to do with a hostile actor or another country… The American people should have confidence in that.” (Watch)
  • DNI Clayton: “Let me tell you what we think this is, and we think that it is with confidence. Lots of institutions, because these vulnerabilities have been identified, are patching. They’re taking their systems down, they’re upgrading them, they’re putting patches in place… This is being done on much larger scale because everybody, and it’s a good news story, everybody recognizes it’s time to upgrade their systems. And as they upgrade them, they’re not coming back as expected in all cases. And in some cases, systems have to hand off to other systems, and those handoffs are not coming back as expected. But this is just an upgrade in patching, an upgrade in systems.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Rubio: “Sometimes when you are going in to fix your system because you’ve identified a vulnerability, it creates a short-term disruption in the way your system works… Companies, which is a good thing, are now immediately sharing vulnerabilities because they don’t want to be accused of covering up something.” (Watch)
  • DNI Clayton: “As a result of SI and the ability to scan systems more quickly, the ability to identify vulnerabilities has increased. That is why it is so incumbent upon all of us to work together to patch, to report vulnerabilities, and it is where the U.S. is leading.” (Watch)
  • DNI Clayton: “Our systems need upgrades. They need patching. We have legacy systems, and they’re more and more interconnected, and they’re handling more and more traffic… Thankfully, the U.S. is leading and is far ahead in that step change in technology… We’re going to come out the other side much better.” (Watch)

Education is among the most important investments we make in America’s future, equipping the next generation with the knowledge, skills, and confidence to lead our country toward greater prosperity.  This American Education Week, my Administration reaffirms its commitment to restoring greatness to our education system, ending the reign of far-left indoctrination in our classrooms, and empowering parents to choose the education that best suits their children’s needs and values.

For decades, American students, teachers, and parents faced an education system that failed to deliver the results they deserved.  Since its inception in 1979, the Department of Education has managed to waste over 3 trillion taxpayer dollars without directly educating students or improving their academic performance.  National assessments in recent years reveal alarming trends, with mathematics and reading scores plummeting as a result of nonsensical leftist policies and Federal Government ineffectiveness.  Our children deserve better.  These results underscore the urgent need to restore common sense to our classrooms and equip our students with the tools they need to build an independent and prosperous future.

Since I returned to office, my Administration has taken decisive action to advance a new era of academic excellence and return educational authority where it belongs:  with States, parents, and local communities.  Through historic Executive Orders expanding educational freedom and opportunity for families, we are reducing federal bureaucracy and putting students and families first.  As part of that effort, I proudly directed the Secretary of Education to facilitate the closure of the Department of Education to put an end to the federal control that has failed generations of American children. 

At the same time, my Executive Orders bar programs that receive Department of Education funds from advancing unlawful “Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion” mandates.  Under my leadership, taxpayers will no longer be burdened with billions of dollars wasted on progressive social experiments and obsolete programs.  We are delivering an education system that shifts the focus from dividing students by race and identity to uniting them around the timeless ideals of advancement through sheer hard work, merit, and excellence.

America’s greatness has always depended on the promise of the next generation.  This week, we recognize the dedicated teachers, devoted parents, and hardworking students who form the foundation of our education system, and we promise them our unwavering commitment to building a system worthy of our Nation’s extraordinary potential.  Together, we will restore greatness to our classrooms, renew confidence in American education, and ensure that every child has the opportunity to pursue their own unique American Dream.

On November 17, 2026 — President Donald J. Trump of the United States, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese of Australia, Prime Minister Narendra Modi of India, and Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae of Japan — met for a Quad Leaders’ Summit in Manila.  This year marks nearly a decade since the Quad was revived and the tenth anniversary of the vision of a Free and Open Indo-Pacific, first articulated by the late Prime Minister Abe Shinzo of Japan in 2016.  A decade on, that vision is stronger than ever.  Together, we have shown that the Quad is a force for good and a partnership of action, committed to peace, stability, and prosperity.  We strongly oppose any destabilizing or unilateral actions that seek to change the status quo, including by force or coercion, which escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and stability.  We express grave concerns about economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions.  We are securing critical supply chains, protecting freedom of navigation and overflight, driving growth through technologies of the future including investments in and deployment of trusted Super Intelligence (SI)*, and responding to disasters with life-saving assistance.  We commit to work together to ensure open, safe, and resilient maritime transit corridors in the Indo-Pacific.  We are working with regional partners to tackle shared challenges and drive opportunities to deliver tangible benefits to the Indo-Pacific.

  • We announce the inaugural Quad Business Leaders’ Forum which is scheduled to be held in early 2027, bringing together business leaders, government officials, and policy experts from Quad countries to foster greater business ties across our private sectors, including the promotion of commercial deals and partnerships critical to the prosperity of the Indo-Pacific.
  • We affirm the importance of the Super Intelligence* Accelerator, announced by our Foreign Ministers in Atlanta.  The Accelerator is intended to coordinate and fund efforts to support trusted Super Intelligence (SI)* access, deployment, and technical assistance across the Indo-Pacific.
  • We are proud to welcome the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration, a new initiative to enhance information sharing and maritime domain awareness.  In 2027, our respective P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft are scheduled to fly in a maritime exercise for the first time in a Quad context, making our seas safer.
  • We are proud of progress under the Quad Partnership for Cable Connectivity and Resilience, which has expanded access to secure and trusted communications infrastructure across the Indo-Pacific.  Today, we welcome an expansion of Australia’s contribution to the Partnership to focus on electricity cables, strengthening regional energy security and connectivity.  We also welcome upcoming undersea cables projects in the Indian Ocean which are intended to strengthen regional connectivity.
  • We acknowledge the rapid increase in the number and scale of cyber incidents in the region and announce enhanced Quad Cybersecurity Cooperation, through which we plan to work together to achieve an open and secure cyberspace.
  • We unequivocally condemn terrorism and violent extremism in all its forms and manifestations, including cross-border terrorism, and commit to strengthening the Quad’s ongoing cooperation on counterterrorism.

We reaffirm our unwavering support for ASEAN centrality and unity.  Together, we are committed to upholding a free and open Indo-Pacific.

* In Australia, India, and Japan, ‘Super Intelligence’ refers to ‘artificial intelligence.’

On November 17, 2026, in Manila, Philippines, President Donald J. Trump and Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul confirmed that the United States of America (“the United States”) and the Kingdom of Thailand (“Thailand”) have reached substantial conclusion in their negotiations for an Agreement Between the United States of America and the Kingdom of Thailand on Reciprocal Trade (“ART”).

The ART will strengthen our bilateral economic relationship and will build upon our longstanding economic relationship, including the Treaty of Amity and Economic Relations Between the Kingdom of Thailand and the United States of America, signed in 1966, and the Trade and Investment Framework Agreement Between the United States of America and the Kingdom of Thailand, signed in 2002.

The United States and Thailand will now begin their respective necessary internal processes to prepare the ART for signature and entry into force. 

IN WITNESS WHEREOF the undersigned, being duly authorized thereto by their respective Governments, have signed this Joint Statement.

DONE in duplicate at Manila, in English, this 17th day of November, 2026.

Traffic fatalities have fallen to the second-lowest level in American history following President Donald J. Trump’s crackdown on illegal alien truck drivers. That good news joins sharp drops in traffic deaths, overdoses, violent crime, and border fatalities after the largest immigration enforcement surge in modern history — while Democrats’ open-border policies left chaos, missing kids, and body counts.

Saving lives is at the heart of President Trump’s border security and law enforcement agenda. At his direction, the Administration is arresting criminal illegals, removing unqualified truck drivers from the roads, and rescuing victims of human trafficking.

Here are six ways President Trump’s immigration policy is saving lives:

It is making America’s roads safer. Traffic deaths dropped sharply in the first half of this year — the second-lowest half-year fatality rate on record. This follows President Trump’s order to enforce English proficiency requirements and review non-domiciled commercial licenses — taking 34,000 drivers out of service for failing basic English standards and revoking more than 31,000 illegally issued licenses. For years, Democrats looked the other way while foreign drivers who could not read road signs or communicate with law enforcement operated 80,000-pound trucks on American highways.

It is crushing the overdose crisis. Overdose deaths fell 11.5% amid record fentanyl seizures and the lowest levels of cross-border drug trafficking in years, driving down fentanyl pill purity. In fact, drug overdose deaths have now declined for 18 straight months under President Trump. After Democrats refused to secure the border and allowed cartels to flood American communities with poison, that pipeline is now being choked off.

It is confronting violent crime and criminal aliens. Violent crime dropped 9.3% in 2025, including an 18.1% drop in murder and nonnegligent manslaughter — the largest annual drop in violent crime ever recorded — while ICE conducted a record 491,000 immigration arrests and 483,000 deportations in FY26. Criminals shielded and released under the previous Administration are now being removed from the country faster than ever before.

It is dramatically lowering deaths at the border. Migrant deaths fell nearly 80% in FY26 from Biden-era peaks as the Trump Administration delivered 18 straight months of zero releases at the southern border and drove illegal crossings down 95% from the Biden-era monthly average. Southwest border apprehensions fell to just a tiny fraction of the more than 1.8 million annually under Biden. The prior Administration’s catch-and-release policies turned the border into a humanitarian disaster; that era is over.

It is bringing endangered children to safety. Approximately 157,000 of the roughly 300,000 unaccompanied migrant children lost under Biden have been located in President Trump’s second term. The scale of the Biden-era failure on missing migrant children remains one of the most serious scandals of that presidency.

It is rescuing victims from human traffickers. The Trump Administration has rescued more than 7,200 children from traffickers and predators (a 42% increase over the previous Administration) and arrested more than 3,500 predators and human traffickers (a 102% increase). Immigration enforcement saves lives; non-enforcement enables exploitation.

This morning, Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy appeared on all five Sunday shows to level with the American people about Friday’s nationwide ground stop. Secretary Duffy laid out the Trump Administration’s decisive actions to isolate the problem and restore the airspace and shared preliminary findings from the investigation.

While Democrats shamefully lie and resist finishing the job, Secretary Duffy also reiterated that the $12.5 billion provided in the Working Families Tax Cuts (which not a single Democrat voted for) was written specifically for radar, radios, and related upgrades — not a new telecom network or software. As President Donald J. Trump made clear, Congress must approve the rest of the funding so the modernization can be finished.

Key exchanges:

  • On the Trump Administration’s immediate response: “We were talking to the President… He said, ‘Whatever resource in any other Department that you need, let me know. You can pull them. I want everybody to work on this’ — because the safety of the traveling public is number one for him, like it is for me.” (State of the Union)
  • On what caused the ground stop: “The telecom in El Dorado, it was an old copper wire that basically was going to be decommissioned. They said it can’t be used anymore, so we were forced by the telecom provider to actually update that copper to fiber and we brought in our routers and did the work, and that’s when we saw the flooding of the network.” (Face the Nation)
  • On the need for Congress to fully fund a modernized air traffic control network: “I have systems that are from the ‘90s. I have radar that are from the ‘60s and ‘70s… [We’re] replacing radar and radios, we’re putting in voice switches, we’re doing all of this work with the $12.5 billion, but one of the biggest problems we continue to see is our network — and the architecture of our network is from 1980. We need a modern technology and architecture. I have AT&T, Verizon, and Lumen all ready to go. We have the architecture ready to build a state-of-the-art telecom system that will give us resiliency. All I need is the money to finish it.” (State of the Union)
  • On what the $12.5 billion downpayment can — and can’t — do: “When I asked for a massive amount of money to fix the system, what the Congress did is they said, ‘Okay, we’ll give you a partial funding, $12.5 billion,’ in the One Big Beautiful Bill, and they were very specific in how we spend it… But what I don’t have money for is a new telecom system. I don’t have money for new software… Let’s finish the job. Let’s not see what happened on Friday. Let’s not let it happen again.” (Face the Nation)
  • On Democrats’ “unspent money” talking point: “Whoever’s saying that, they have to actually read the bill that gave me the money. It was very specific… There’s no money for towers. Our towers are old. Our air traffic controllers oftentimes don’t have elevators or HVAC… Their roofs leak. Let’s build a new system that is worthy to be called American.” (State of the Union)
  • On the broad consensus for fully modernizing the system: “If you don’t give us the resources, we can’t complete the job… This is the most bipartisan thing in all of Washington — Democrats, Republicans, the President, everyone agrees on this. Let’s just do it. Do it for the American people.” (Meet the Press)
  • On Democrats’ push to pull money from border security: “We should be able to keep our borders safe, we should be able to deport illegals, and we should be able to invest in safe air travel in America. We should be able to invest in new networks, invest in software. We can do all things; we don’t have to pick one versus the other.” (Fox News Sunday)
  • On the safety of American air travel: “It is the safest air system in the world, bar none… It’s going to remain safe. But let’s not lie to each other — we have to make investments into a network that has been neglected for decades.” (Meet the Press)
  • On delivering results: “President Trump and I are going to fix it.” (Meet the Press)

On Friday night, Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy and Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin briefed reporters after a nationwide FAA ground stop caused by instability in the nation’s decades-old air traffic control systems. The failure stemmed from overloaded 1980s-era equipment, with zero evidence of a cyberattack. President Trump has already secured $12.5 billion toward a full rebuild; the Administration is urging Congress to provide the remaining funding so this never happens again.
 
On what happened — and how the FAA kept every flight safe:

  • Secretary Duffy: “At 3:36 p.m., we experienced instability for our radar and our communications in our centers and our TRACONs across the country… At that point, we issued a ground stop. We had over 3,500 airplanes in the air; they all engaged and, last time I looked, we had less than 400 in the airspace. As they were all coming into safely land, we navigated it with our well-known procedures that we have when these incidents happen… We didn’t lose all telecom. We didn’t lose all radar. But that instability, because of an abundance of caution and making sure we keep the American flyer safe, we did the ground stop.” (Watch)

On an air traffic control system stuck in the 1980s:

  • Secretary Duffy: “What we have is an incredibly old air traffic control system… The President, for the last year, has been asking Congress to fully fund a full build of a brand-new air traffic control system. We have TDM telecom; this is analog telecom. Our switches, our routers, actually got overloaded with data… Because of that, we shut the system down. I have already replaced some of those switches with President Trump — and our new IP switches did not go down. It’s the old hardware that went down. I think the question for the American people is: do you want your Congress to fund this? President Trump has asked for the money, he has asked the Congress on a bipartisan approach to give us the resources to build a state-of-the-art air traffic control system. Let’s not do a patchwork fix to a system that’s critical to every single family.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Duffy: “We have old switches, old routers. We use 1980s little copper lines. It’s an old system that went down, and went down everywhere. It got overloaded… By the way, none of your networks run on 1980 technology. You all got fiber, state-of-the-art, high-speed networks… But not the FAA.” (Watch)

On reports of a cyberattack:

  • Secretary Mullin: “We have seen zero evidence that this was a cyberattack or an SI attack.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Mullin: “There is nothing that indicates [a cyberattack]… It appears that this was mechanically driven; however, we’re still looking.” (Watch)

On years of delay and the need for full funding:

  • Secretary Duffy: “This is an emergency. I want Congress to give us emergency funding. This is bipartisan; this is American. I want $50 billion. President Trump is a builder; he’s going to build this network and deliver for the American people, but the President can’t deliver for America unless the Congress delivers the money to make it happen.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Mullin: “This is a national security risk. We just saw what took place when we have vulnerabilities and we have old systems… Our air traffic control system is outdated, and it hasn’t been a priority from Congress… This is what happens when Congress kicks the can down the road.” (Watch)

On building a brand-new system — starting now:

  • Secretary Duffy: “I did get partial funding through One Big Beautiful Bill — I got $12.5 billion, and with that money, we are spending it and spending it well. But the Congress at the time knew that that was not going to be enough… We now have an opportunity in an emergency funding bill before the end of the year to give the money.” (Watch)
  • Secretary Duffy: “This is not going to get done overnight… but when do you want to start it? America, when do you want to start building a brand-new system? Well, you have a team with President Trump that actually is building it right now, but we don’t have full funding.” (Watch)

Under President Donald J. Trump’s leadership, the Administration has delivered historic results for the American people in just 21 months through executive action alone. The promise of America has been quickly reignited under the President’s common-sense leadership, making America the hottest nation in the world and reviving the American Dream. Crime has plummeted, merit is restored, burdensome red tape is gone, and American energy is unleashed. 

President Trump will never stop delivering on his promises to Make America Great Again. Time and time again, he has defied the naysayers, achieving what they deem as impossible to deliver results that improve the lives of the American people. 

Exercising his executive authority, the President has: 

  • Executed a record-setting 147 Executive Orders in his first 100 days—more than any other President in history—and over 290 Executive Orders since January 2025, delivering on his promises of a more prosperous and secure America. 
  • Delivered the most secure border in history, enforcing an extraordinary crackdown on illegal immigration, resulting in negative net migration to the U.S. for the first time in over half a century. 
    • Terminated welfare for illegal aliens across government programs, including public housing benefits, food stamps, and small business loans. American taxpayer benefits are for Americans only, not illegal aliens.Strengthened H-1B enforcement to protect the jobs of hardworking Americans and prevent visa abuse.

  • Delivered the largest drop in violent crime in American history in 2025, and preliminary 2026 data shows it is falling even further. 
    • In one year, violent crime saw its largest decline in history; murders fell over 18% to the lowest rate ever seen, and robberies fell more than 18%.
    • Property crimes, rapes, and aggravated assaults all dropped as well in 2025.
    • Captured all of the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted fugitives — 2.5 times as many as the entire previous four-year Administration — and six of the FBI’s Most Wanted Fraudsters.
  • Cracked down on fraud, waste, and corruption across the federal government at an unprecedented rate, and restored integrity to federal programs designed to help Americans in need.
    • Uncovered more than $260 billion in fraud of taxpayer dollars and stopped $72 billion a year, breaking up large-scale fraud schemes and seeing through that fraudsters are brought to justice.
    • The Trump Administration has stopped fraudulent payments before they go out the door, detected high-risk fraud trends, and shut down suspected fraudulent providers and retailers.
  • Ended illegal and discriminatory diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) practices across government, education, and the private sector. 
    • Reformed higher education by ending race-based discrimination in admissions and employment, DEI programming, and antisemitism.
    • Secured historic settlements of hundreds of millions with elite universities for their DEI practices, including Columbia, Brown, Cornell, the University of Virginia, Northwestern, and the University of North Carolina.

  • Enacted President Trump’s record-shattering deregulation agenda, saving a family of four over $17,500—or $1.5 trillion total—in one year alone by cutting over 400 regulations.
    • Thanks to these cuts, the Trump Administration is the first in history to reduce the regulatory burden on the American people.

With more than two years to go, President Trump will not hesitate to use the power and authority of the Executive Branch to deliver historic victories for the American people.
